parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime documents tier-1/tier-2 exposures: since March 2022, trans women swept up in mass raids are held in ordinary prisons by birth sex with forced hair-cutting, punishment drills, and HIV-care denial, one woman still imprisoned; police show 'blatant refusal' to cooperate in LGBT death investigations; prison rules forbid effeminate behaviour and guards target gender-nonconforming detainees; a 2013 survey found 85% believe attacking a trans person is acceptable. Mitigants are real but thin: a hate-crime statute (30-60 years), the 2020 first-ever conviction of three officers, a judge freeing one detainee, and 2009 health anti-discrimination guidelines. Paper protections coexist with documented state custody abuse and societal violence acceptance, placing this below 0.35 exclusion-tier anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: No gender identity recognition; no domestic mechanism aligning foreign documents. Document mismatch at checks would force outing, with no recognition framework guiding officials.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy during exception-regime security sweeps could escalate into arrest and birth-sex prison placement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Since March 2022 exception regime, trans women arbitrarily captured in raids held in ordinary prisons with no gender-identity accommodation: forced hair shaving, punishment drills, one still imprisoned after judge freed another. Police refuse to cooperate in LGBT death investigations.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A judge freed one woman after ~4 months finding the arrest unsupported; habeas-type judicial review operated once.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Mass raids plus document/presentation-based stops feed directly into birth-sex custody with documented abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Birth-sex prison placement documented as state practice; prison rules forbid effeminate dress/behaviour; police, soldiers and guards target gender-nonconforming men with searches, theft, sexual assault. No subnational protective regime recorded; only capital-scoped items are the 2020 conviction and rainbow crossroads.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Capital-specific: first homicide conviction of three officers (20 years). Rainbow paintings are symbolic only.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Capital pockets of tolerance do not alter the national prison/custody regime a detained visitor enters.

care_services.exposure: Hospital specialists dismiss trans patients' problems as side effects of being trans; longer waits or denied care; no hormone or surgery protocols; HIV clinic access denied to imprisoned trans woman.
care_services.protection: 2009 health ministry guidelines banning LGBT/HIV discrimination in health services and 2009 HIV plan prohibition.
care_services.interaction: Paper guidance did not prevent the documented 2022 denial of HIV care in custody.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police, soldiers and prison guards are documented perpetrators targeting effeminate presentation. 2013 survey: 85% believe attacking a trans person on identity grounds is acceptable; 62% reject homosexuality. Gang violence includes trans-targeted assault, sexual assault and extortion for safety.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2015 hate-crime law (3-6 years for GI-motivated offences; 30-60 years for bias killings); 2018 institutional policy allowing LGBT discrimination complaints.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hate-crime statutes exist but international reports document systemic failure to investigate and police non-cooperation, so paper protection rarely reaches the street.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented family conversion therapy, expulsion, and school dropout for LGBT youth — resident sphere; a travelling parent of a gender-diverse minor could face hostile social attitudes (85% violence acceptance).
minors_guardians.interaction: If a travelling family member were detained, birth-sex placement with no accommodation would apply equally.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Roughly 500 reported hate crimes 1998-2015 (many unreported); international organisation finds the state fails to address violence, driving asylum claims; police obstruction documented. Severity tier-3 societal hostility with thin recourse.
street_violence_police_response.protection: One 2020 landmark conviction of three officers showed prosecution can succeed; enhanced bias-killing penalty on books.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A single conviction amid two decades of non-cooperation signals uneven, not reliable, protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Whether the hate-crime framework produced further convictions is unsourced; one trans woman remains imprisoned; oversight repeatedly records unremedied abuse.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts showed independence once (2020 conviction; judge freeing detainee); 2022 supreme court name-law ruling (unimplemented).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working judiciary exists but sits alongside documented institutional failure to investigate, so remedies are sporadic.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case: documented sweeps with coerced statements, failing magistrates, credible capital clause, and no successful remedy. Here a judge freed a detainee, three officers received 20 years, and no capital pathway exists, so the rating sits above 0.15-C despite comparable custody abuse.

Closest match: birth-sex prison placement with assault risk, arrests for presentation, slow remedies, execution excluded, reform uncertain. This dossier adds state raid captures under an exception regime and 85% public acceptance of attacking trans people, pulling slightly below 0.25-C.

Higher than this case: police checks there end in hours-long release with fines, no custodial abuse. This dossier documents imprisonment with forced shaving, punishment drills and care denial, plus police non-cooperation in killings — materially more severe.
Far higher: administrative secondary screening and refused admission with appeal desks. This dossier's state custody abuse and documented societal violence acceptance place it several tiers lower.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime pairs real but fragile protections — a hate-crime statute, one landmark police-killer conviction, a judge who freed a wrongly held trans woman, 2009 health non-discrimination guidance — with heavier documented exposures: birth-sex prison placement and abuse under an exception regime active since 2022, police refusal to investigate LGBT killings, prison rules criminalising effeminacy enforced by guards and soldiers, restricted emergency care, gangs extorting LGBT people, and a survey finding 85% of residents consider attacking a trans person acceptable. Paper protections are outweighed by state-imposed custody exposure and unremedied institutional failure, so the visitor who is outed or swept up faces imprisonment under hostile conditions with unreliable recourse. Adult-alone and travelling-family exposures are similar, the latter additionally touching a hostile social climate.
